what: TensorFMA32 (25 Oct 2026): the multiply-add as built and flow M, the chip diagram's twelfth flow. The edition's data, applied by build_facts.py on top of the research files: facts (new; dz = the deep zoom's, fetched from ladder-data.json), facts_changed (was: the value it was made against; now: the edition's), num and onum (the numbers the page prints), scales and scales_changed (the deep zoom's scenes), comp (flow M's panel), asks, and tfma (the flow's worked example, RTL signal values and toggle maps). Sources: Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1, with core-et's open Erbium RTL where it has the same modules, and the lab's own data.

asks.ask_detail: an experiment: the same flips on the gate-level netlist
asks.part: the avalanche in physical wires (Flow M, TensorFMA32)
asks.what_is_inferred: The physical count for the average flip (about 300 wires in the tree) is the RTL count divided by 3.5 names per wire; a gate-level run checked it only for three bits of b with a = π and 1.0, at zero delay.
asks.what_settles_it: Replay the 192,000 single-bit flips on the gate-level netlist of lane 0 (the earlier gate-level harness takes a stream of micro-ops), at zero delay and with gate delays, and count physical toggles per stage.

size.fma.benc.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder; tfma.benc
size.fma.benc.statement: A Booth encoder: about 1.5 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. Ten cells, three of them big drivers.

size.fma.col.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder; size.lib.fa
size.fma.col.statement: One column of a level: about 2 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. One 4:2 compressor, about two full adders.

size.fma.lvl.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder; tfma.asbuilt.cells
size.fma.lvl.statement: One level of the Wallace tree: about 30 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. A logical drawing: the compressors are synthesized logic placed by tools.

size.fma.psel.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder; tfma.psel
size.fma.psel.statement: One partial-product bit: about 500 nm across, the width of the view that frames it. Two cells.

size.lib.cmos.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder; size.lib.nand2, size.lib.aoi21
size.lib.cmos.statement: A static CMOS gate: about 300 nm across, the width of the view that frames it. A compound gate is 3 to 6 gate pitches (171-342 nm) wide in one 240 nm row (n7.cells).

tfma.asbuilt.cells.cards_txt: the design (RTL and netlists), not a card
tfma.asbuilt.cells.note: The tape-out's own netlist is not among the files; this one is synthesized from the same RTL with the tape-out flow.
tfma.asbuilt.cells.source: Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1: lane 0 of a netlist synthesized from the ET-SoC-1's RTL with its tape-out flow, traced cone by cone from the RTL's register names, and the cells' transistor netlists
tfma.asbuilt.cells.statement: One lane's multiplier as built: 4,487 cells and 49,755 transistors, each with 2 fins. The Booth path is about 21,300 transistors, the tree's four levels 22,110 (level 1 10,153, level 2 4,513, level 3 4,537, level 4 with the adder's first layer 2,907), the product adder 5,718. The tree has no 4:2 cell: 248 full-adder cells (162 mirror type, 86 transmission-gate type) and XOR, majority and compound gates.

tfma.avg.note: A bit of a costs more: a is Booth-recoded, so one flip re-selects one or two whole rows (an odd bit sits in two groups); a bit of b changes one bit in each non-zero row. A bit of c never reaches the tree (156 in the unit). Physical wires: RTL names ÷ 3.5 (tfma.names), checked against the gate-level run for bits of b (tfma.flip.gate).
tfma.avg.source: a Verilator simulation of the multiply-add's RTL (one lane's txfma_top, the module core-et's Erbium branch also has; FMADD_PS, round to nearest even; it matches an exact fp32 fused multiply-add on 3,000 of 3,000 cases), research for this page, 23 October 2026: 192,000 single-bit flips (a and b normally distributed; c = 0, 1, 100 or random)
tfma.avg.statement: Averaged over all 46 fraction bits of a and b, each flipped alone in 2,000 random operand sets: 1,037 RTL signal bits toggle in the Wallace tree (1,227 for a bit of a, 848 for a bit of b), 1,106 with the Booth rows, 2,059 in the whole unit; about 300 physical wires in the tree.

tfma.benc.source: Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1: the hand-drawn schematics of the multiply-add's datapath and their gate netlist
tfma.benc.statement: Esperanto's hand-drawn Booth encoder: one = y(2i) ⊕ y(2i−1); two = NOR(XNOR(y(2i+1), y(2i)), one); neg = y(2i+1); the row's inverted sign = neg ⊕ NOT((one + two) · sx). Two XORs, an XNOR, a NOR, an OR-AND-INVERT gate and five buffers, three of them big drivers for the lines that run along the row's 33 bits: 232 transistors, 144 of them in the drivers.

tfma.booth.fp32.source: a bit-exact model of the RTL, checked on 20,000 vectors against a Verilator build of the RTL files (this page's research, 23 Oct 2026)
tfma.booth.fp32.statement: In fp32, rows 1-4 are always zero (a's low 8 bits are zero), row 16 can only be −2b, −b or 0 and row 17 is always +b: at most 13 rows carry data, about 10 for a random a (π gives 10, 1.0 gives 2).

tfma.booth.rows.note: In fp32 a's low 8 bits are zero, so rows 1-4 are always zero: at most 13 rows carry data (a = 1.0 gives 2 non-zero rows, a = π 10).
tfma.booth.rows.source: Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1 (its RTL, its RTL review and drawings of the partial products); the same modules in core-et's open Erbium RTL: rtl/shire/minion/vpu/txfma_7s/txfma_booth_ppg_32r4_norm.v, txfma_booth_ppg_32r4.v, txfma_booth_ppg_32r4_msb.v, txfma_wallace1.v
tfma.booth.rows.statement: a's 24-bit significand sits in bits 31-8 of a 32-bit multiplier. Radix-4 Booth recoding reads it three bits at a time (bits 2k−1, 2k−2 and 2k−3 for row k) and makes 16 rows of 33 bits, each 0, +b, +2b, −b or −2b (000 and 111 give a zero row). A negative row is only inverted; its +1 goes into a separate carry-in row, and the rows' sign extensions are replaced by their inverted signs, constant ones and a 'magic' 1 at bit 33 of row 1. Row 17 adds b once more for the multiplier's top bit. 18 rows enter the tree.

tfma.clocked.note: The RTL view: 1,739 of 2,071 register bits load per multiply-add.
tfma.clocked.source: a gate-level simulation of lane 0 of a netlist synthesized from the ET-SoC-1's RTL with its tape-out flow (zero delay), with every clock gate's enable evaluated from its netlist cone (Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1)
tfma.clocked.statement: A random-data multiply-add clocks 1,586 of the lane's 1,851 multiply-add flip-flops; a zero operand word, 15.

tfma.cmp42.source: Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1 (its RTL and RTL review); the same module in core-et's open Erbium RTL: rtl/shire/minion/vpu/txfma_7s/txfma_4_2_compressor.v:20-21
tfma.cmp42.statement: txfma_4_2_compressor is two full adders: the first adds x0, x1 and x2 into s0 and a sideways carry cout; the second adds s0, x3 and the carry from the column to the right into s and c. cout = majority(x0, x1, x2) does not depend on the carry coming in; x0 + x1 + x2 + x3 + cin = s + 2(c + cout).

tfma.csa.source: Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1 (its RTL); the same module in core-et's open Erbium RTL: rtl/shire/minion/vpu/txfma_7s/txfma_csa.v:19-20
tfma.csa.statement: txfma_csa, the RTL's full adder: sum = a ⊕ b ⊕ cin; carry = a·b + a·cin + b·cin.

tfma.depth.cards_txt: the design (RTL and netlists), not a card
tfma.depth.source: lane 0 of a netlist synthesized from the ET-SoC-1's RTL with its tape-out flow (Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1; research for this page)
tfma.depth.statement: The longest register-to-register path is 16 cells in f1 (the Booth selection by depth 9, level 1 at depths 6-14, level 2 at 10-16) and 23 in f2 (levels 3-4 by depth 10, then the adder).

tfma.example.note: With bit 8 of a's fraction flipped instead, Booth row 9 changes from 0 to −b: 23 partial-product bits enter the tree at once, and the unit toggles 2,154 signal bits, 1,255 of them in the Wallace tree.
tfma.example.source: a Verilator simulation of the multiply-add's RTL (one lane's txfma_top, the module core-et's Erbium branch also has; FMADD_PS, round to nearest even; it matches an exact fp32 fused multiply-add on 3,000 of 3,000 cases), research for this page, 23 October 2026; the operands are the lab's E60 case
tfma.example.statement: The worked example: a = π (0x40490fdb), b = 1.2345678 (0x3f9e0651), c = 100 (0x42c80000). Flipping bit 11 of b's fraction makes b = 1.2348119 (0x3f9e0e51): the product goes from 3.8785091 to 3.8792761 and the result from 103.87851 (0x42cfc1cc) to 103.87927 (0x42cfc230), 8 of its 32 bits.

tfma.fa.mirror.cards_txt: the design (RTL and netlists), not a card
tfma.fa.mirror.source: Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1 (the cells' transistor netlists); N. Weste and D. Harris, CMOS VLSI Design, 4th ed. (Addison-Wesley 2011), ch. 11 (the mirror adder)
tfma.fa.mirror.statement: The tree's full-adder cell is the textbook 28-transistor mirror adder: a carry stage of 10 transistors that makes NOT carry, a sum stage of 14 that reuses it, and an inverter on each output. Each pull-up is the same series-parallel arrangement as its pull-down.

tfma.fa.tg.cards_txt: the design (RTL and netlists), not a card
tfma.fa.tg.source: Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1: the cells' transistor netlists, and lane 0 of a netlist synthesized from the ET-SoC-1's RTL with its tape-out flow (86 of 248 full-adder cells)
tfma.fa.tg.statement: About a third of the tree's full adders are a 36-transistor transmission-gate type: transmission gates steered by a pass b or NOT b (an XNOR), then the carry in steers the sum and the carry.

tfma.flip.energy.note: Glitches, which a zero-delay model leaves out, add about 40 % to the tree's energy (tfma.glitch). For scale: a random fp32 multiply-add measures 5.8 pJ above idle on the cards (e-tfma-fp32).
tfma.flip.energy.source: a gate-level simulation of lane 0 of a netlist synthesized from the ET-SoC-1's RTL with its tape-out flow (zero delay), priced with its cells' energies at the typical corner, interpolated to 0.517 V (Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1)
tfma.flip.energy.statement: Priced with the cells' energies at the minion's 0.517 V, flipping such a bit of b (with a = π) on every multiply-add costs about 0.11-0.13 pJ more in the multiplier: the Booth rows, the tree and the product adder.

tfma.flip.gate.source: a gate-level simulation of lane 0 of a netlist synthesized from the ET-SoC-1's RTL with its tape-out flow (zero delay), the lab's E60 case 'b bit 11, a = π' (Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1); compared with the RTL simulation of the research for this page
tfma.flip.gate.statement: In a gate-level simulation of the netlist the same flip toggles 381 physical wires in the Booth rows, the tree, its register and the product adder: 129 in f1 (19 of them the register's flip-flops) and 252 in f2 (16 of them the product's).

tfma.flip.stages.note: Zero delay, so no glitches. Every bit of every named signal in every module is counted, as a simulator's toggle count does; for the distinct count, bits with identical waveforms over a long training stream count once. RTL names are not wires: a physical wire carries about 3.5 RTL names in the tree and 2.55 in the whole unit (tfma.names).
tfma.flip.stages.source: a Verilator simulation of the multiply-add's RTL (one lane's txfma_top, the module core-et's Erbium branch also has; FMADD_PS, round to nearest even; it matches an exact fp32 fused multiply-add on 3,000 of 3,000 cases), research for this page, 23 October 2026
tfma.flip.stages.statement: Flipping that bit changes 1,946 named RTL signal bits as the difference passes through the unit: 3 on the operand bus and 8 in f0 (11 with the bus), 409 in f1, 639 in f2, 235 in f3, 284 in f4, 173 in f5 and 195 in f6. 875 of them are in the Wallace tree (its four levels and its register) and 48 in the Booth rows. Counted once per wire, they are 482 distinct nets.

tfma.flop.cards_txt: the design (RTL and netlists), not a card
tfma.flop.source: Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1 (the cells' transistor netlists)
tfma.flop.statement: A flip-flop in transistors: 22 without scan (a clock inverter, a clocked input inverter, two latches with clocked keepers and a transmission gate between them, an output inverter), 30 in the scan version the silicon uses; 10 of its gates sit on the clock.

tfma.frame.source: Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1 (its RTL); the same definitions in core-et's open Erbium RTL: rtl/inc/txfma_defines.vh
tfma.frame.statement: The unit works in one 64-bit fixed-point frame: the 48-bit product of two 24-bit significands lands in bits 61-14, and the addition and everything after it use the 52 bits from 63 down to 12.

tfma.glitch.source: a gate-level simulation of lane 0 of a netlist synthesized from the ET-SoC-1's RTL with its tape-out flow: its timed pass (event-driven, inertial delays) against the zero-delay one (Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1)
tfma.glitch.statement: With gate delays the multiplier tree makes about 1.5 times as many toggles as at zero delay (1,871 against 1,244 physical toggles per random multiply-add) and spends about 1.4 times the energy.

tfma.hand.note: The hand design's netlist has the 7-stage split: the Booth rows and tree levels 1-2 in f1, levels 3-4 and a Ladner-Fischer adder in f2, the aligner in f3, the 52-bit adder and the leading-one anticipator in f4, the normalising shifter in f5 and the round incrementer in f6.
tfma.hand.source: Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1: the hand-drawn schematics of the multiply-add's datapath and their gate netlist, and the tape-out flow, which never sets the hand-placed option; the option in core-et's open Erbium RTL: rtl/shire/minion/vpu/txfma_7s/txfma_top.v (MINION_USE_MMI_TXFMA)
tfma.hand.statement: Esperanto also drew the multiply-add's datapath by hand: a hand-placed version of the same 7-stage design, an alternative to the synthesized RTL that a define selects and the tape-out never set. It uses a 4:2-compressor cell (241 per lane; a later copy has 246), 47 full adders and 42 half adders at the ragged edges. The silicon is the synthesized RTL.

tfma.icg.cards_txt: the design (RTL and netlists), not a card
tfma.icg.source: Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1: its RTL (the same clock gates in core-et's open Erbium RTL: rtl/shire/minion/vpu/txfma_7s/txfmafrac_top.v), lane 0 of a netlist synthesized from the ET-SoC-1's RTL with its tape-out flow, and the cells' transistor netlists
tfma.icg.statement: 27 clock gates per lane's multiply-add: the lane's own, 13 that Esperanto's RTL places (one per operand register, one for the transcendental-ROM registers, the control word, each stage f0-f5 and two for the multiply-type registers) and 13 that synthesis added. The smallest clock gate is 22 transistors: a latch that holds the enable while the clock is high, a NAND and an inverter.

tfma.lab.note: The simulator's toggle coverage, the lab's tool, misses the compressor cells' input ports and counts transient values while the model settles (30 counted where 2 changes happened), so its counts inside the tree are not reliable.
tfma.lab.source: a Verilator simulation of the multiply-add's RTL (one lane's txfma_top, the module core-et's Erbium branch also has; FMADD_PS, round to nearest even; it matches an exact fp32 fused multiply-add on 3,000 of 3,000 cases), research for this page, 23 October 2026, with the lab's stream pattern (rtl-sim/fma_toggle: 16×16×16 random tiles, a and b normal, 2 seeds, 3 accumulator scales); the lab's count: docs/reports/data/2026-09-21-horace-aifoundry2/toggles_all.json
tfma.lab.statement: The lab's count of 21,331 toggles per random multiply-add was not reproduced: on the same RTL and the same random TensorFMA32 pattern, this page's research counts 7,160-7,470 per multiply-add (5,820-6,090 with the lab's own counting tool), 55 % of them in the tree rather than 85 %.

tfma.maj.cards_txt: the design (RTL and netlists), not a card
tfma.maj.source: Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1 (the cells' transistor netlists)
tfma.maj.statement: The majority (carry) gate is the mirror adder's carry stage alone: 10 transistors with an inverted output, 12 with an inverter added.

tfma.mdp.size.source: Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1 (a 2018 presentation of the design)
tfma.mdp.size.statement: A July 2018 snapshot of the hand-placed significand datapath of an earlier TXFMA, stages F1-F4, measured 78.3 × 30.72 µm (work in progress).

tfma.names.cards_txt: the design (RTL and netlists), not a card
tfma.names.source: a synthesis of the vector lane that kept every module (Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1)
tfma.names.statement: Names per physical net in a synthesis of the lane that kept its hierarchy: 2.55 over the whole multiply-add, 3.70 in the first tree module (txfma_wallace1) and 3.48 in the second.

tfma.operands.source: Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1 (its RTL); the same in core-et's open Erbium RTL: rtl/shire/minion/vpu/vpu_tensorfma.v, vpu_bypass.v and txfma_7s/txfma_f1.v (.mplr and .mpcnd)
tfma.operands.statement: In a TensorFMA32, a is one TenA element broadcast to all 8 lanes and is the multiplier that gets Booth-recoded; b is the lane's own TenB element, the multiplicand; c is the accumulator from the lane's register file. The first pass issues a multiply (FMUL_PS), every later pass a multiply-add (FMADD_PS).

tfma.owner.note: The lab's figure is its 21,331 counted toggles per random multiply-add divided by the 20.3 bits of a and b that change between consecutive multiply-adds: an average over a stream, not one flip's cascade (tfma.owner.why). Counted directly on the RTL, an isolated flip toggles 1,037 signal bits in the tree on average (tfma.avg).
tfma.owner.source: the owner, 23 Oct 2026; the same figure as the lab's RTL toggle model (tools/claims-v3/dtf/README.md, S15: 21,331 counted toggles ÷ 20.3 bits on txfma_top)
tfma.owner.statement: One input bit flip in the 7-stage TensorFMA32 triggers an avalanche of about 1,050 toggles across the Wallace tree.

tfma.owner.why.source: the lab's RTL toggle model: tools/claims-v3/dtf/README.md (S15) and docs/reports/data/2026-09-21-horace-aifoundry2/toggles_all.json; a Verilator simulation of the multiply-add's RTL (one lane's txfma_top, the module core-et's Erbium branch also has; FMADD_PS, round to nearest even; it matches an exact fp32 fused multiply-add on 3,000 of 3,000 cases), research for this page, 23 October 2026: 20.0 bits of a and b change per multiply-add in the lab's stream pattern
tfma.owner.why.statement: The owner's ~1,050 is an average over a random stream: the lab's 21,331 counted toggles per random multiply-add divided by the ~20 bits of a and b that change from one multiply-add to the next (about 1,067), not one flipped bit's cascade.

tfma.padd.cards_txt: the design (RTL and netlists), not a card
tfma.padd.source: Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1: its RTL (the same in core-et's open Erbium RTL: rtl/shire/minion/vpu/txfma_7s/txfma_f2.v, txfma_adder.v), a synthesis of the vector lane, and the hand-drawn schematics of the multiply-add's datapath
tfma.padd.statement: The product adder is 64 bits, written as a + b in the RTL. A synthesis of the lane made it a parallel-prefix adder of about 700 cells, at most 11 gates deep (a ripple adder would be about 64); Esperanto's hand design was a Ladner-Fischer prefix adder at twice the bit pitch.

tfma.psel.source: Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1: the hand-drawn schematics of the multiply-add's datapath and their gate netlist
tfma.psel.statement: Esperanto's hand-drawn partial-product bit: pp = (one · b(j) + two · b(j−1)) ⊕ neg, an AND-OR-INVERT gate (2-2) and an XNOR, 18 transistors; the hand design's f1 has 528 of them (16 rows × 33 bits), 247 with a NOR that zeroes the bit in fp16-pair mode.

tfma.reg12.cards_txt: the design (RTL and netlists), not a card
tfma.reg12.source: Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1: its RTL (the same in core-et's open Erbium RTL: rtl/shire/minion/vpu/txfma_7s/txfma_f1.v), and lane 0 of a netlist synthesized from the ET-SoC-1's RTL with its tape-out flow (the tape-out's own netlist is not among the files; its flip-flops are the bits a model of the RTL calls non-constant, except three sign bits synthesis merged)
tfma.reg12.statement: Between f1 and f2 a register holds the tree's four rows and the two rows that wait for level 4: 353 bits in the RTL (4 × 64 + 33 + 32 + 32). Synthesis keeps 253 flip-flops (constant bits pruned), of which 205 can change in fp32.

tfma.regs.stage.cards_txt: the design (RTL and netlists), not a card
tfma.regs.stage.source: Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1: its RTL, elaborated (research for this page, 23 Oct 2026), and lane 0 of a netlist synthesized from the ET-SoC-1's RTL with its tape-out flow, by the stage each register feeds
tfma.regs.stage.statement: The register that starts each stage, in RTL bits (flip-flops in lane 0 after synthesis): f0 255 (229), f1 223 (213), f2 606 (492), f3 340 (322), f4 263 (248), f5 238 (213), f6 146 (134): 2,071 bits, 1,851 flip-flops.

tfma.sel.asbuilt.cards_txt: the design (RTL and netlists), not a card
tfma.sel.asbuilt.source: Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1: lane 0 of a netlist synthesized from the ET-SoC-1's RTL with its tape-out flow (one row traced by hand, the rest by logical support), and an earlier synthesis of the vector lane
tfma.sel.asbuilt.statement: As built, each partial-product bit is two inverting multiplexers steered by bits of b (one makes the ±b term of this bit, the other the ±2b term of the next) and a NAND or NOR that joins them: about 24-26 transistors. The row's encoder decodes a's three bits into four one-hot lines (+1, −1, +2, −2) from two-input NORs and NANDs. An earlier synthesis used an AND-OR-INVERT (2-2), an OR-AND-INVERT (2-2-1) and an inverter per bit: 20 transistors.

tfma.side.source: Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1 (its RTL); the same in core-et's open Erbium RTL: rtl/shire/minion/vpu/txfma_7s/txfma_f3.v, txfma_f4.v, txfma_f5.v
tfma.side.statement: In f3 a 32-bit integer and min-max register loads the product's top 32 bits on every fp32 multiply-add and carries them to f4 and f5, where nothing reads them: 64 register-bit loads a multiply-add for nothing.

tfma.stages.note: Lane stages F2 to F8; the operands are read in F1. Checked on a simulation of the RTL: 3,000 random and corner-case multiply-adds and 23 boundary cases agree with an exact fp32 fused multiply-add, result and flags.
tfma.stages.source: Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1 (its RTL and stage diagrams); the same stages in core-et's open Erbium RTL: rtl/shire/minion/vpu/txfma_7s/txfma_f0.v … txfma_f6.v, txfma_top.v; external/core-et/docs/Minion VPU Specification.pdf §2.2.3
tfma.stages.statement: The TensorFMA32 multiply-add (each vector lane's TXFMA) is a 7-stage pipeline, f0 to f6: f0 captures the operands; f1 recodes a and adds its 16 Booth rows of b down to 4 (tree levels 1-2); f2 finishes the tree (levels 3-4) and adds the last two rows into the product; f3 lines the product up with c and merges them; f4 adds them while it anticipates the leading one; f5 normalises and decides the rounding; f6 rounds and writes the result. A new multiply-add enters every cycle; each result leaves 7 cycles later.

tfma.tree.arrays.source: Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1 (its RTL); the same in core-et's open Erbium RTL: rtl/shire/minion/vpu/txfma_7s/txfma_wallace1.v:81-88, txfma_wallace2.v:29-32, txfma_4_2_compressor_array.v:17-21
tfma.tree.arrays.statement: 8 arrays of 64 4:2 compressors (4 + 2 + 1 + 1): 512 compressors, 1,024 full adders in the RTL. In an array, column i takes a carry from column i − 1; its own sideways carry does not depend on it, so nothing ripples. Between levels the carry row moves one column left.

tfma.tree.fp32.source: the bit-exact model of the RTL (this page's research)
tfma.tree.fp32.statement: In fp32, 314 of the tree's compressors have an input that can change, the first level-1 array (rows 1-4) never switches, and 1,090 of the tree's nets can toggle.

tfma.tree.levels.note: The RTL calls it a Wallace tree; it is a regular tree of 4:2 compressors with no 3:2 level, two levels in each of f1 and f2.
tfma.tree.levels.source: Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1 (its RTL and stage diagrams); the same in core-et's open Erbium RTL: rtl/shire/minion/vpu/txfma_7s/txfma_wallace1.v:81-88, txfma_wallace2.v:29-32, txfma_f1.v, txfma_f2.v
tfma.tree.levels.statement: The tree adds the rows in four levels of 64-bit arrays of 4:2 compressors. In f1, level 1 (four arrays: rows 1-4, 5-8, 9-12, 13-16) makes 8 rows and level 2 (two arrays) 4, which a register holds. In f2, level 3 (one array) makes 2, and level 4 adds those 2, row 17 and the sign row into 2. A 64-bit adder in f2 adds the last two into the product.

tfma.tree.synth.cards_txt: the design (RTL and netlists), not a card
tfma.tree.synth.source: a synthesis of the vector lane that kept every module (Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1); a model of the RTL predicts the same, column for column
tfma.tree.synth.statement: Synthesis keeps 377 of the 512 compressors (745 of the 1,024 full adders: 485 with three inputs that can change, 149 half adders, 111 single-input ones): level 1 four bands of 39 columns (0-38, 8-46, 16-54, 24-62), level 2 two of 47 (0-46, 16-62), level 3 63 (0-62), level 4 all 64.

tfma.underflow.source: Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1 (its RTL); the same in core-et's open Erbium RTL: rtl/shire/minion/vpu/txfma_7s/txfma_c6.v; external/core-et/docs/Minion VPU Specification.pdf §2.2.3.9; a Verilator simulation of the multiply-add's RTL (one lane's txfma_top, the module core-et's Erbium branch also has; FMADD_PS, round to nearest even; it matches an exact fp32 fused multiply-add on 3,000 of 3,000 cases), research for this page, 23 October 2026, six constructed cases
tfma.underflow.statement: Results below 2^-126 flush to zero, as denormal inputs read as zero. The RTL judges 'below' after rounding: a result just under 2^-126 that rounds up comes back as 2^-126 (0x00800000) with only the inexact flag, where the VPU specification says before rounding.

tfma.xnor.cards_txt: the design (RTL and netlists), not a card
tfma.xnor.source: Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1 (the cells' transistor netlists)
tfma.xnor.statement: The tree's two-input XNOR is a NAND (4 transistors) and an OR-AND-INVERT gate (6): 10 transistors, no transmission gates; its XOR twin is a NOR and an AND-OR-INVERT gate.

tfma.zero.note: The lane's own clock gate keeps running (vpu_lane.v).
tfma.zero.source: Esperanto's design files for the ET-SoC-1 (its RTL); the same in core-et's open Erbium RTL: rtl/shire/minion/vpu/vpu_ctrl.v (ex_fma_gate_mask) and txfma_7s/txfmafrac_top.v
tfma.zero.statement: Zero gating: in a TensorFMA's accumulate passes a lane gets no valid bit when its a or b word is exactly 0x00000000 (a zero a gates all 8 lanes, a zero b its own lane), and then none of the unit's stage clock gates opens. −0.0, denormals and the first pass are not gated.

now.note: Zeros clock almost nothing: a zero operand word withholds the micro-op's valid bit, so the multiply-add's stage clock gates stay shut (15 flip-flops clocked per lane-op instead of 1,586; tfma.zero, tfma.clocked).

was.source: estimate from the RTL's structure and the textbook full adder (J. Rabaey, A. Chandrakasan, B. Nikolic, Digital Integrated Circuits, 2nd ed. (Prentice Hall 2003), ch. 11)
was.statement: Reducing 17 rows of about 33 bits to 2 takes on the order of 500 full-adder equivalents; at about 28 transistors per full adder, some 14,000 transistors, about 20,000 with the Booth selectors.

fma.benc.blurb: Esperanto's hand-drawn encoder for one row: three bits of a in; the row's select lines (one for ±b, two for ±2b, neg) and its inverted sign bit out, with big drivers for the lines that run along the row.
fma.benc.name: A Booth encoder, as Esperanto drew it
fma.benc.note: a hand design of the same 7-stage datapath, never taped out: ten cells, 232 transistors

fma.col.blurb: One bit position of one array: four bits of the same weight and a carry from the column to the right come in; a sum (same weight) and two carries (twice the weight) go out, one sideways to the next column, one down to the next level.
fma.col.name: One column of a level: one 4:2 compressor
fma.col.note: a logical drawing: one compressor and its neighbours, about two full adders wide each

fma.lvl.blurb: One level halves the rows: each group of four rows goes through a row of 64 4:2 compressors, one per bit position, and comes out as a sum row and a carry row. Each compressor passes a carry sideways to the next column, which does not wait for it.
fma.lvl.name: One level of the Wallace tree
fma.lvl.note: a logical drawing: the compressors are synthesized logic placed by tools, not a row on silicon

fma.psel.blurb: Esperanto's hand-drawn bit of a Booth row: an AND-OR-INVERT gate picks b's bit j (for ±b) or bit j−1 (for ±2b), and an XNOR inverts it for a negative row: 18 transistors.
fma.psel.name: One partial-product bit, as Esperanto drew it

lib.cmos.blurb: Any static CMOS gate from its function: n-type transistors in series for AND and in parallel for OR pull the output down; p-type ones in the opposite arrangement pull it up.
lib.cmos.name: A static CMOS gate in transistors
lib.cmos.note: a compound gate is 3 to 6 gate pitches (171-342 nm) wide in one 240 nm row (order of magnitude; n7.cells)

lib.fa.tr.blurb: The tree's full-adder cell: a carry stage of 10 transistors computes NOT carry, a sum stage of 14 reuses it, and two inverters drive the outputs: 28 transistors, the textbook mirror adder.
lib.fa.tr.name: A full adder in transistors: the mirror adder
lib.fa.tr.note: order of magnitude: a full-adder cell spans several gate pitches

now.blurb: Every bit of weight 2^40 on its way down the tree: twelve Booth-row bits in fp32 into three compressors of level 1, then two in level 2, the register, one in level 3 and one in level 4, which also takes row 17's bit and the sign row's. Carries leave for column 41 and arrive from column 39.
now.name: Column 40 of the tree, all four levels
now.note: a logical drawing of the eight compressor positions of one column (4 + 2 + 1 + 1)

was.blurb: One bit position of the multiplier: its 17 partial-product bits pass down through layers of 4:2 compressors. Each passes a carry to the next column and takes one from the column before, so the whole tree works in parallel.
was.name: One column of the compressor tree
was.note: order of magnitude: one bit-column of a tree some 40 um wide

now.blurb: Adding 64-bit numbers quickly means not waiting for a carry to ripple through 64 positions: the fastest prefix adders compute all the carries in about six levels of logic.
now.name: Fast (parallel-prefix) adder
now.note: a 64-bit adder: tens of um (order of magnitude)

was.blurb: Adding 64-bit numbers quickly means not waiting for a carry to ripple through 64 positions: the fastest prefix adders compute all the carries in about six levels of logic.
was.name: Fast (parallel-prefix) adder
was.note: a 64-bit adder: tens of um (order of magnitude)

now.blurb: Looks at three overlapping bits of the multiplier and chooses 0, +/-1 or +/-2 times the multiplicand for that row: two multiplier bits per row instead of one.
now.name: Booth encoder and partial-product selector

was.blurb: Looks at three overlapping bits of the multiplier and chooses 0, +/-1 or +/-2 times the multiplicand for that row: two multiplier bits per row instead of one.
was.name: Booth encoder and partial-product selector

now.blurb: Two full adders in a chain: four bits of a column and a carry in become a sum and two carries. Its sideways carry does not depend on the carry coming in, so a row of them adds without a ripple.
now.name: 4:2 compressor

was.blurb: Takes four bits of a column (and a carry in) and gives two bits out: the step of a multiplier's adder tree that halves the rows at each level.
was.name: 4:2 compressor

now.blurb: Adds three bits and gives a sum bit and a carry bit: the brick of every adder and multiplier.
now.name: Full adder

was.blurb: Adds three bits and gives a sum bit and a carry bit: the brick of every adder and multiplier.
was.name: Full adder

now.blurb: Computes c + a × b on 32-bit floats, rounded once, in a pipeline of seven stages, f0 to f6: a new multiply-add enters every cycle and each result leaves 7 cycles later. Its multiplier (f1 and f2) is a radix-4 Booth recoder and a Wallace tree of 4:2 compressors; then the sum is aligned, added, normalised and rounded.
now.name: Multiply-add unit (TXFMA): TensorFMA32 in seven stages
now.note: order of magnitude: synthesized logic placed among the lane's other units; its multiplier alone is about 50,000 transistors as built, and a hand-placed version of an earlier design's significand datapath measured 78 × 31 µm

was.blurb: Computes a x b + c on 32-bit floating-point numbers (or two 16-bit ones) in one pass, rounding only once. Inside are a multiplier array, an adder, and circuits that line up and normalise the exponents.
was.name: Fused multiply-add unit (TXFMA)
was.note: order of magnitude; the multiplier array alone is some 20,000 transistors (see below)

now.blurb: a's significand is read three bits at a time; each group picks 0, +b, +2b, −b or −2b for one row, so 16 rows (and a 17th for a's top bit) replace 32. The rows, shifted two places each, go to the Wallace tree.
now.name: The Booth multiplier: rows of b chosen by a
now.note: order of magnitude: the Booth path is about 21,300 transistors as built

was.blurb: Multiplication is many shifted additions. Radix-4 Booth encoding looks at the multiplier two bits at a time, halving the number of rows to add: 17 rows for a 32-bit multiplier.
was.name: Booth encoders and partial products

now.blurb: Floating-point numbers must be lined up by their exponents before adding, and the result shifted back and rounded: a shifter, a wide adder, a leading-zero counter and a rounding adder.
now.name: Align, add, normalise, round

was.blurb: Floating-point numbers must be lined up by their exponents before adding, and the result shifted back and rounded: a shifter, a wide adder, a leading-zero counter and a rounding adder.
was.name: Align, add, normalise, round

now.blurb: Adds the 18 rows (16 Booth rows, row 17 and a sign row) down to two in four levels of 64-wide arrays of 4:2 compressors: 16 → 8 → 4 in f1, a register, then 4 → 2 and 2 + row 17 + the sign row → 2 in f2. Most of the multiplier's area and most of its switching.
now.name: The Wallace tree as built: four levels of 4:2 compressors
now.note: order of magnitude: about 22,000 transistors (the four levels, one lane, as built), spread by the placement tool through the multiply-add

was.blurb: The 17 rows are added in a tree of small adders that turn every four bits of a column into two, level after level, until two rows remain for one final adder. This is most of the multiplier's area and most of its switching.
was.name: Compressor tree (Wallace tree of 4:2 compressors)

gate.source: a gate-level simulation of lane 0 of a netlist synthesized from the RTL with the tape-out flow (zero delay, physical toggles per micro-op)
